Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s vision or eyes.
Parent: Our child has astigmatism, which makes it hard for him to see clearly. We're worried it might affect his schoolwork.

Doctor: Please tell us about problems with your child's hearing or ears.
Parent: He always turns the TV volume up really high. It's like he can't hear well unless it's blasting. I'm getting a bit concerned it could be a sign of a hearing problem.

Doctor: Please tell us about the problems with your child’s teeth.
Parent: We have to take him to the dentist a lot because his teeth are prone to problems. The dentist says he needs more frequent visits than average to keep them healthy.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s heart.
Parent: There's a structural issue with his heart that the doctors are monitoring. They say it's an abnormality that we should keep an eye on, but so far, it hasn't caused him any pain or discomfort.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child's hormones.
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about any neurological problem your child has (brain, nerves, muscle tone, fits).
Parent: He seems a bit clumsy compared to other kids. When he runs or plays, he often trips or stumbles. The doctors mentioned it could be related to coordination issues.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child's kidneys.
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s immune system (ability to fight infection and vaccination responses).
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about problems with your child’s gastrointestinal system (feeding, stomach， bowel).
Parent: Constipation has been a real issue for our son. He struggles to go to the bathroom regularly and it causes him a lot of distress.

Parent: He was born with shorter fingers than usual， which sometimes makes it tricky for him to hold onto things or do certain tasks that require finger dexterity.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a structural issue with his heart that requires monitoring. 
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences constipation, which causes distress.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Feeding difficulties and lack of interest in feeding can be significant and long-lasting in some individuals with KBG syndrome.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient appears a bit clumsy and has trouble holding onto things or doing tasks requiring finger dexterity due to a potential coordination issue.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, which typically respond to anti-epileptic treatments.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has had issues with fluid buildup in the ear, leading to conductive hearing loss.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has astigmatism, making it hard for him to see clearly.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Individuals with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism and short- or long sightedness (myopia and hypermetropia).

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient requires more frequent dental check-ups due to tooth problems.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient needs extra help in school, indicating possible learning difficulties.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Education outcomes vary, with some children obtaining qualifications and others needing more support.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient is described as being a bit clumsy and has trouble with finger dexterity, suggesting potential coordination issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Developmental delays and various behavioral differences are commonly reported in individuals with KBG syndrome.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has an unusual structure of his spinal bones, which could lead to an increased curvature of the spine (scoliosis).
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Various skeletal anomalies can be present in individuals with KBG syndrome, including delayed fontanelle closure and hip dysplasia.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
a) Recommendations for screening: Regular dental check-ups, hearing reviews, and palatal reviews.
b) Recommendations for treatments: Monitoring of heart conditions, treatment of tethered cord, management of palatal abnormalities, and consideration of hormonal therapies as per clinical findings.

# CLINICAL REFERENCE GUIDELINES
''''''
What is KBG syndrome?
KBG syndrome was first described in 1975, and its name is derived from the initials of the first three patients reported with the condition.  People with KBG syndrome have a characteristic (and sometimes subtle) facial appearance, very large permanent teeth, and variable degrees of developmental delay, learning difficulties and behavioural differences. Because the facial features can be subtle and are not always present, the diagnosis may not be  made until the permanent teeth have come through. Other features seen in some affected individuals include conductive hearing loss, undescended testes in boys, seizures, skeletal anomalies and short stature. KBG syndrome is caused by changes (variants) in, or a deletion of, the ANKRD11 gene in chromosome  16 (band q24.3). Most affected people are the first person in their family to carry the gene change, but a small proportion have inherited it from a parent, who is likely to have features of KBG syndrome. The facial features can be subtle and are not always present, but other features may include conductive hearing loss, undescended testes in boys, seizures, skeletal anomalies and short stature. KBG syndrome is one of the most prevalent causes of syndromic developmental delay.  This guide is designed to help families and healthcare professionals looking after people affected by KBG syndrome. It contains information about the cause, the ways in which it can affect people and suggestions about the help and management that can benefit people with this condition.
What causes KBG syndrome?
KBG syndrome is caused by one copy of the ANKRD11 gene not functioning properly. This may be due to a change (variant) within the gene that disrupts its function, or to the loss (deletion) of the whole gene or part of it. The other copy is unaffected.
Why did this happen?
When children are conceived, their parents’ genetic material (DNA) is copied in the egg and sperm that makes a new child. The biological copying method is not perfect and occasionally random, rare changes occur in the genetic code of children that are not seen in the DNA of their parents. KBG syndrome occurs when one of these random, rare changes occurs in the ANKRD11 gene in chromosome 16. This happens naturally and is not due to the biological parents’ diet, environment or lifestyle. In most people with KBG syndrome, the genetic change was a random (or “de novo”) change, meaning the change occurred for the first time in that family in the affected individual. 
Occasionally, one parent may have the same change (variant) and pass it on to their child. No one should be blamed for variants in their DNA and no parent is at fault when a new DNA change occurs in their child.
Can it happen again?
The possibility of having another child affected by a rare gene disorder depends on the genetic code of the parents. In most families, the genetic change has happened for the first time in the child with KBG syndrome. We call this a ‘de novo’ change. In this situation, when the parents are unaffected, the chances of having another child with the same condition are very low (usually less than 1%). 
One reason why there is some residual chance of recurrence is due to a rare phenomenon called germline mosaicism. This is when a parent carries a genetic change, but it is limited to some of their egg or sperm cells. The genetic change would not, therefore, be detected in the parents’ blood tests. Unique publishes a short general guide to mosaicism that covers this phenomenon. If a parent has KBG syndrome, the chances of passing the condition on to a child are much higher at 50%, or 1 chance in 2, as the parent could either pass on their altered copy of the gene or the unaffected copy. This inheritance pattern is called autosomal dominant (because the change is on an autosomal chromosome and an outcome can be seen if only one copy of the gene is altered). Unique publishes a separate guide to single gene disorders -autosomal dominant inheritance. Each family situation is different, and a clinical geneticist or genetic counsellor can give specific advice for your family.
Development:
Developmental delay has been reported in almost all children with KBG syndrome. The degree of delay ranges from mild (in most) to severe (in few). Developmental “milestones”, including rolling, sitting, walking, playing with toys, using cutlery, using zips and buttons, and toilet training, are often delayed, although there is a wide range of eventual ability, with some children acquiring mobility and other skills around the same age as “typical” children and others showing more obvious delay.

Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, though most go to a mainstream primary school. b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: As an infant, the patient had trouble feeding properly, which caused concern at the time.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences epilepsy and requires medication to manage his seizures.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, which typically respond to the usual anti-epileptic treatments.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has had otitis media, which has caused some discomfort and affected his hearing temporarily until it was treated.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many individuals with KBG syndrome have had issues with otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has difficulty seeing clearly and requires corrective lenses.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Individuals with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism and squint (strabismus).

a) How this affects the patient: N/A

a) How this affects the patient: The patient has an unusual structure of their spinal bones and an increased curvature of the spine (scoliosis).

a) How this affects the patient: The patient is extremely picky about food textures, leading to challenges during mealtime.

a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences episodes of staring off into space for brief periods, which can be concerning but are generally under control.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, which can be managed with various treatment options.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has experienced otitis media or glue ear, which may contribute to her speech delay and hearing difficulties.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has hypermetropia, which affects her ability to see things up close.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism and short- or long sightedness (myopia and hypermetropia).

a) How this affects the patient: The patient requires gentle brushing techniques and regular dental check-ups to maintain oral health.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient struggles with physical fatigue, making participation in physically demanding activities challenging.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Educationally, children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help, with some benefiting from mainstream settings and others requiring specialized support.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a septal defect that requires monitoring and potential surgery.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences feeding difficulties, including trouble swallowing certain foods and making faces when eating.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient is described as being a bit clumsy and lacks coordination, particularly when running or playing.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, which typically respond to anti-epileptic treatments.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has experienced issues with fluid in her ear, which is being monitored and treated.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have feeding difficulties and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has astigmatism, where the front of the eye is not perfectly rounded, causing blurry vision.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Individuals with KBG syndrome may have vision problems such as myopia (nearsightedness), hypermetropia (far-sightedness), and squint (strabismus), where the eyes do not look in the same direction.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient requires regular dental check-ups and has been advised to maintain good oral hygiene.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Dental care is crucial, and regular visits to the dentist are essential to prevent tooth decay and other issues.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has required additional support in school, with some needing more assistance than others.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Education outcomes vary, with some children obtaining qualifications and others requiring support from specialist settings.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient exhibits clumsiness and lack of coordination, which impacts her overall development.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Developmental delays are commonly reported, with some children acquiring mobility and other skills around the same age as “typical” children and others showing more obvious delay.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can lead to an increased curvature of the spine (scoliosis).
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A study showed that 11% of children with KBG syndrome have tethered cord, which can cause pain and weakness in the legs, urinary and bowel issues, sacral dimple, and an unusual gait.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
a) Recommendations for respiratory: N/A
b) Recommendations for cardiovascular: Regular monitoring and potential surgery for a septal defect.
c) Recommendations for gastrointestinal: Work on making mealtime easier for the patient.
d) Recommendations for immunology: N/A
e) Recommendations for neurology: Monitoring and treatment of seizures.
f) Recommendations for ear nose throat: Addressing fluid buildup and ensuring proper ventilation.
g) Recommendations for optics: N/A
h) Recommendations for dermatology: N/A
i) Recommendations for dental: Regular dental check-ups and maintaining good oral hygiene.
j) Recommendations for education: Providing additional support as needed.
k) Recommendations for behaviour and development: Addressing clumsiness and lack of coordination.
l) Recommendations for skeletal: Considering monitoring for possible complications related to spinal structures.
m) Recommendations for recommendations for screening and treatments: N/A

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a septal defect that is being monitored by a cardiologist. Regular check-ups are scheduled to assess the development and necessity of intervention.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes, with some requiring surgery and others needing monitoring.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences difficulty swallowing and getting food down smoothly during meals, leading to frustration.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Feeding difficulties are common in individuals with KBG syndrome, with some infants having feeding challenges and others experiencing constipation or irregular bowel movements.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient falls more often than peers, which is concerning and stressful for the family.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Approximately 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome experience seizures, which can be managed with various treatments.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has experienced otitis media or glue ear, which has led to fluid accumulation in the ear and necessitated treatment.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many individuals with KBG syndrome have had issues with fluid buildup in the ear, making regular monitoring and timely interventions crucial.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has astigmatism, which affects his vision clarity, and corrective measures are being considered to address this issue.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Individuals with KBG syndrome may exhibit vision problems such as myopia, hypermetropia, and astigmatism, which could impact their daily activities and need periodic evaluation and treatment.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences difficulty eating and swallowing, which impacts his comfort and willingness to engage in mealtime.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Dental care is essential, and frequent visits to the dentist are recommended to prevent complications and ensure proper oral hygiene.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient requires additional support in school due to various challenges, including falling, frustration during meals, and speech delays.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Educationally, children with KBG syndrome may need accommodations to assist with learning and development, and some may benefit from specialized settings or support.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient displays behavioral tendencies and developmental delays compared to his peers.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Developmentally, individuals with KBG syndrome may face challenges in areas such as self-help skills, communication, and overall cognitive function, but with appropriate support, many children and adults with KBG syndrome lead fulfilling lives.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which could potentially influence their posture and gait, requiring observation and potential intervention if significant issues arise.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Skeletally, some individuals with KBG syndrome may experience hip dysplasia, tethered cord, or other structural anomalies that could impact their mobility and alignment, necessitating regular monitoring and possible surgical intervention if necessary.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
a) Recommendations for respiratory screening: N/A
b) Recommendations for cardiovascular screening: Regular cardiology check-ups are recommended to monitor the septal defect and ensure proper development.
c) Recommendations for hearing screening: Hearing should be carefully and regularly checked starting from infancy to identify and address potential issues early.
d) Recommendations for eyesight (ophthalmology) screening: Ophthalmological evaluations are advised to detect and treat vision problems such as astigmatism and myopia.
e) Recommendations for undescended testes screening: If testes were not descended in infancy, periodic monitoring and consideration of surgical intervention may be warranted.
f) Recommendations for skeletal screening: Wrist-to-height ratio testing and hip, spine, and skull X-rays should be conducted to evaluate for abnormalities and monitor bone development.
g) Recommendations for teeth screening: Frequent dental visits are essential to prevent cavities and ensure proper tooth health.
h) Recommendations for feeding screening: Feeding difficulties should be closely monitored and addressed through a multidisciplinary approach.
i) Recommendations for cardiac screening: As per current knowledge, the patient continues to receive monitoring for his heart condition.
j) Recommendations for tethered cord screening: Any concerns regarding tethered cord should be evaluated through MRI to determine the extent of the anomaly and appropriate treatment plan.
k) Recommendations for palatal screening: The specialist mentioned palatal abnormalities, and ongoing assessment is necessary to understand their implications and develop an effective intervention strategy.
l) Recommendations for neurological screening: Falls and associated injuries should be closely monitored, and supportive therapies may be beneficial.
m) Recommendations for gastrointestinal screening: Regular meal-time assessments and exploration of potential dietary triggers for discomfort should inform future care plans.
n) Recommendations for immunology screening: N/A
o) Recommendations for genetics screening: N/A
	p) Recommendations for physical therapy: Physiotherapy sessions focused on improving posture and reducing fall risks can provide significant benefits.
	q) Recommendations for occupational therapy: Occupational therapy aimed at enhancing functional independence and daily living skills can greatly enhance the patient’s quality of life.
	r) Recommendations for speech therapy: Speech therapy to address any articulation or clarity issues can lead to improved communication abilities.

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient exhibits rapid breathing upon exertion, suggesting possible cardiac concerns.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of individuals with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to heart valves, holes in heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experienced feeding difficulties as a baby, including spitting up and reflux, which resolved somewhat but left occasional discomfort post-eating.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient appears less coordinated compared to peers, experiencing confusion and difficulty maintaining balance during physical activities.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of individuals with KBG syndrome have seizures, which typically respond to anti-epileptic treatments.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient requires frequent ear infections, including otitis media and glue ear, which impact his hearing and overall health.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Individuals with KBG syndrome are more likely to have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can lead to conductive hearing loss and affect their hearing and speech development.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has hypermetropia, which affects his vision and leads to discomfort when reading or watching television.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism and squint (strabismus), which may impact their daily life and learning.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences tooth sensitivity and requires frequent dental visits to address various issues, including cavities and gum disease.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Dental care is crucial, and regular check-ups are essential to prevent complications and maintain oral health.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient benefits from additional support in school, requiring accommodations and interventions to assist with learning and social development.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Educationally, individuals with KBG syndrome vary in success, with some obtaining qualifications and others needing more support. However, many adults with KBG syndrome have gone on to further education or independent lives.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient displays developmental delays and behavioral differences, including hypotonia (low muscle tone), palatal abnormalities, and speech delay.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Developmentally, individuals with KBG syndrome may face challenges in areas such as mobility, self-help skills, and cognitive abilities. However, with appropriate support, many children with KBG syndrome achieve independence and lead fulfilling lives.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can lead to an increased curvature of the spine (scoliosis), and hip dysplasia, which affects his movement and posture.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Skeletally, individuals with KBG syndrome may experience hip dysplasia, tethered cord, and an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can impact their mobility and posture.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
a) Recommendations for screening: Regular dental check-ups, hearing reviews, and periodic vision assessments are recommended.
b) Recommendations for treatments: Monitoring for heart conditions, treatment of sensorineural hearing loss, management of palatal abnormalities, consideration of neurorehabilitation therapies, and evaluation for potential tethered cord issues are suggested.

a) How this affects the patient: The patient gets tired quickly when running around or playing physically, indicating potential neurological issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, which typically respond to anti-epileptic treatments.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has experienced fluid in his ear, affecting his hearing.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

a) How this affects the patient: The patient has hypermetropia, which affects his eyesight and prevents him from seeing things up close.

a) How this affects the patient: N/A

a) How this affects the patient: The patient has difficulty eating due to tooth sensitivity and frequent toothaches.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Dental concerns such as weak enamel and need for frequent dental check-ups are common in individuals with KBG syndrome.

a) How this affects the patient: The patient needs extra help in school and may require support from EHCP or specialized settings.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Education outcomes vary, with some children obtaining qualifications and others needing more support.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Individuals with KBG syndrome may exhibit various behavioral differences such as autism spectrum disorder (ASD), ADHD, or anxiety.

a) Recommendations for screening: Regular dental check-ups, hearing reviews, and palatal reviews.

a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences otitis media or glue ear, which can lead to conductive hearing loss and affect her hearing and speech development.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many children with KBG syndrome have palatal abnormalities, which can impact their speech development and feeding.

a) How this affects the patient: The patient has astigmatism, where her eyes do not focus correctly, leading to blurred vision and requiring corrective measures.

a) Recommendations for screening: Regular dental check-ups, hearing reviews, and vision assessments.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences sensitivity to cold temperatures, particularly affecting his teeth.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Feeding difficulties and palatal abnormalities can lead to various ear infections and discomfort.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a heart valve issue that requires periodic monitoring to ensure everything remains stable.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient is picky about food and some textures make eating difficult.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences seizures and has neurological issues, requiring careful monitoring and medication adherence.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, which typically respond to anti-epileptic treatments.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a history of otitis media or glue ear, which can lead to conductive hearing loss and require regular check-ups.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Feeding difficulties and palatal abnormalities can be associated with KBG syndrome, affecting speech development and feeding.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has astigmatism, where the front of the eye is not perfectly rounded, causing blurry vision.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Squint (strabismus), where the eyes do not look in the same direction, can occasionally be a feature, and treatment may include patching, exercises, glasses, and surgery.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient needs regular dental check-ups to prevent tooth decay and maintain overall oral health.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Dental concerns such as weak enamel and frequent visits to the dentist are common, and careful brushing is essential.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has varying levels of educational attainment, with some obtaining qualifications and others needing more support.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Educationally, there is a wide range of outcomes, with some children staying in mainstream education and others requiring additional support.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient exhibits developmental delays and has speech delay, as well as palatal abnormalities and seizures.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Developmentally, there is a wide range of abilities, with some children acquiring mobility and other skills around the same age as “typical” children and others showing more obvious delay.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can cause scoliosis, and there are various skeletal anomalies that may develop.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: KBG syndrome is associated with an increased incidence of skeletal anomalies, including hip dysplasia, tethered cord, and asymmetric hip creases, which may affect movement and posture.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
a) Recommendations for screening: Regular dental check-ups, hearing reviews, and vision assessments.
b) Recommendations for treatments: Monitoring of heart valve issues, treatment of palatal abnormalities, seizure management, and consideration of hormonal interventions as needed.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences challenges during mealtimes, with occasional episodes of upset stomach or feeling sick after consuming certain foods.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Feeding difficulties are common in individuals with KBG syndrome, and some may require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences falls more often than expected for a child her age, possibly due to clumsiness or imbalance.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, which typically respond to anti-epileptic treatments.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has experienced glue ear in the past, and while it has resolved, regular monitoring is ongoing to prevent future occurrences.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasal tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences vision problems such as astigmatism and myopia, requiring regular check-ups with an optometrist.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Individuals with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism and myopia, and regular eye examinations are recommended.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient requires regular dental check-ups to maintain oral health and prevent tooth decay.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Dental issues are common in KBG syndrome, and regular dental visits are crucial to prevent infections and maintain overall oral hygiene.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient benefits from additional support in school, including physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioral therapy to address developmental delays and support academic progress.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Education outcomes vary among individuals with KBG syndrome, with some children obtaining qualifications and others needing more support. Overall, a combination of mainstream and specialized settings can provide comprehensive assistance.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient exhibits developmental delays, taking longer to achieve milestones such as sitting, walking, and using cutlery and zips.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Developmental delay is a hallmark of KBG syndrome, with a wide range of abilities among affected individuals, including those with small ANKRD11 deletions or variants.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can lead to an increased curvature of the spine (scoliosis), and hip dysplasia, which may require monitoring and treatment.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: KBG syndrome is associated with various skeletal anomalies, including an increased curvature of the spine, hip dysplasia, and tethered cord, which may impact mobility and posture.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
a) Recommendations for screening: Regular dental check-ups, hearing reviews, and periodic monitoring for heart conditions.
b) Recommendations for treatments: Monitoring and treating septal defects, managing hormonal imbalances, providing physical therapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioral therapy as needed.

The child has difficulty chewing harder foods such as meats or tough vegetables, and avoids them due to pain in the teeth or jaws.
The child has a septal defect, which is an opening in the wall between the two upper chambers of the heart, and is being monitored by cardiologists.
The child occasionally has episodes where he stares off into space and appears unresponsive for a few seconds.
Mealtimes are challenging for the child, who becomes frustrated if food is not to his preference or if he is not hungry at the time of feeding, making mealtime stressful.
The child's movement and coordination are slightly different from those of his peers, with noticeable issues in balance that affect physical play and interaction.
The child's speech development is delayed compared to expected milestones for his age, as he speaks less and less clearly than other children in his class.

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient requires heart check-ups, indicating potential heart conditions.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient struggles with eating, making mealtimes hard.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Feeding difficulties are common in individuals with KBG syndrome, with some requiring short-term nasogastric tube feeding.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has tethered cord, which may lead to complications such as sacral dimple and asymmetric gait.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Approximately 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome experience seizures, which typically respond to anti-epileptic treatments.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences otitis media, a buildup of fluid in the ear, which may contribute to hearing difficulties.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has myopia and hypermetropia, which affect his vision.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Individuals with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism and squint (strabismus).

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient requires frequent dental check-ups and has various tooth-related issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Dental concerns are common in KBG syndrome, including weak enamel and possible need for grommet insertions and hearing aids.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has challenges in school, needing extra help and potentially struggling with certain subjects or tasks.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Education outcomes vary widely among individuals with KBG syndrome, with some obtaining qualifications and others requiring support in mainstream settings.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient exhibits developmental delays and behavioral differences, including speech delay and palatal abnormalities.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Developmental delay is widespread in KBG syndrome, with varying levels of academic achievement and overall functionality.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which may lead to scoliosis and hip dysplasia.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Subtle anomalies of the skull and spine are occasionally observed in KBG syndrome, affecting posture and movement.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
a) Recommendations for screening: Regular dental check-ups, periodic heart check-ups, and consideration for additional hormonal, neurological, and genetic testing as per clinical findings.
b) Recommendations for treatments: Monitoring for tethered cord, addressing palatal abnormalities, managing feeding difficulties, considering corrective surgeries for hip dysplasia and scoliosis, and ongoing speech therapy to support developmental delays.

## 1) RESPIRATORY

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient requires regular heart check-ups as a precautionary measure, indicating potential heart conditions that need monitoring.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes, with some requiring surgery.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences challenges with eating, being picky about food and some foods disagreeing with her, suggesting possible dietary sensitivities or preferences.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Feeding difficulties and lack of interest in feeding can be significant and long-lasting in some individuals with KBG syndrome.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient appears to be clumsier than her peers, with poor coordination and balance, and has difficulty expressing herself effectively, leading to frustration.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, which typically respond to anti-epileptic treatments.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient gets overwhelmed in noisy environments, suggesting potential otitis media or glue ear, where fluid buildup in the ear could exacerbate her discomfort.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has speech delay and vision problems such as astigmatism and short- or long sightedness, which may be linked to her overall health and development.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Individuals with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism and short- or long sightedness, and squint (strabismus), where the eyes do not look in the same direction.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient needs to visit the dentist frequently due to cavities and tooth decay, indicating ongoing dental care needs.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Dental issues such as cavities and tooth decay are common, and regular dental check-ups are crucial to prevent further complications.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has challenges with expression and communication, which can lead to frustration and hinder her academic performance.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Educationally, some individuals with KBG syndrome may require additional support and some benefit from specialized settings, while others can thrive in mainstream settings with appropriate support.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient exhibits developmental delays and lacks clarity in communicating her thoughts and needs, contributing to frustration and behavioral challenges.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Developmentally, there is variability, with some children acquiring mobility and other skills around the same age as “typical” children and others showing more obvious delay. 

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can lead to an increased curvature of the spine (scoliosis), and palatal abnormalities that may affect her speech development and feeding.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: KBG syndrome is associated with various skeletal anomalies, including an unusual structure of the spinal bones, hip dysplasia, and tethered cord, which can impact mobility and posture.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
a) Recommendations for screening: Regular heart check-ups to monitor potential heart conditions.
b) Recommendations for treatments: N/A

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experienced feeding challenges as a baby, including poor feeding patterns and discomfort after feeding.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient was slower to reach certain milestones like walking or sitting compared to other kids, but with support and patience, he got there eventually.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, which typically respond to the usual anti-epileptic treatments.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has had otitis media and glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many individuals with KBG syndrome have had issues with otitis media or glue ear, which can lead to conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences astigmatism, where the front of the eye is not perfectly rounded, causing blurry vision.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Individuals with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism and short- or long sightedness (myopia and hypermetropia).

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A

a) Recommendations for screening: Regular dental check-ups, hearing reviews at age 5, and periodic cardiology evaluations.

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences tiredness more quickly than other kids her age, even after brief physical activity, suggesting potential respiratory issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient gets tired more quickly than other kids her age, indicating possible cardiac issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient doesn't gain weight as fast as other kids, and the doctor mentioned possibly an issue with her tummy not working right.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient falls more often than other children, especially when running or walking.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, and some may have neurological issues such as autism spectrum disorder (ASD), ADHD, or anxiety.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has had issues with fluid in the ear, which may contribute to her hearing difficulties.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Feeding difficulties and palatal abnormalities can worsen hearing and speech development in individuals with KBG syndrome.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has astigmatism, where the front of her eye is not perfectly rounded, causing blurry vision.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Squint (strabismus), where the eyes do not look in the same direction, can occasionally be a feature, affecting vision and alignment.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient requires frequent dental visits due to tooth decay, necessitating early intervention and monitoring.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Dental issues are common, including weak enamel and the need for frequent check-ups and treatment.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has difficulty keeping up with physically demanding activities and may need additional support in school.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Education outcomes vary widely, with some children obtaining qualifications and others requiring more support.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient exhibits developmental delays, including slow weight gain and difficulty maintaining balance and coordination.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Developmental delay is a common feature, with some children showing significant delay and others demonstrating more typical development.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which may lead to an increased curvature of the spine (scoliosis), and hip dysplasia, which affects movement and posture.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Individuals with KBG syndrome may experience various skeletal anomalies, including delayed fontanelle closure, tethered cord, and hip dysplasia.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
a) Recommendations for screening: Regular dental check-ups, hearing reviews, and periodic monitoring for heart conditions.
b) Recommendations for treatments: Addressing palatal abnormalities, managing seizures, providing physiotherapy and occupational therapy, and considering hormonal interventions as needed.

consultation:
Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s vision or eyes.
Parent: Our son has mentioned struggling to see the board at school, especially when the teacher writes in small letters or from a distance. We've noticed this issue for a while now, and it seems to affect his ability to follow lessons comfortably. He often squints or leans forward to get a better view.

Doctor: Please tell us about problems with your child's hearing or ears.
Parent: There are times when our child doesn't respond immediately when called. It's as if he didn't hear us, even when we're standing right next to him. This has happened both at home and in quieter environments, so we're concerned it might be related to his hearing.

Doctor: Please tell us about the problems with your child’s teeth.
Parent: His teeth seem to break or chip very easily. Even minor accidents, like biting into something hard or a slight knock against another tooth, can cause damage. We've had to take him to the dentist more frequently than usual because of this issue.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s heart.
Parent: Yes, our child was born with a septal defect. We've been working closely with cardiologists to monitor the condition and ensure it doesn't worsen over time. So far, the treatments and lifestyle adjustments have helped manage the issue effectively.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child's hormones.
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about any neurological problem your child has (brain, nerves, muscle tone, fits).
Parent: Our child gets tired quickly during physical activity. Simple tasks like playing outside or running around with friends can leave him exhausted sooner than his peers. This has been noticeable since he started engaging in more active play.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child's kidneys.
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s immune system (ability to fight infection and vaccination responses).
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about problems with your child’s gastrointestinal system (feeding, stomach, bowel).
Parent: Our child has a feeding aversion. Certain textures or smells of food can put him off completely. Mealtime can be challenging, and we've had to work with him to find foods he's comfortable eating.

Doctor: Please use this box to tell us about any other medical problems that you haven’t been able to mention above.
Parent: In addition to the issues already mentioned, our child seems behind other children in development. His fontanelle also took longer to close than typical, which was another concern we've been monitoring. These developmental delays and physical differences have required us to adapt his education and activities to better suit his needs.

## 1) RESPIRATORY

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient breathes faster than expected during playtime, suggesting potential cardiac issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has trouble digesting certain foods and experiences discomfort during meals.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences epileptic seizures, which are controlled with medication.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, which typically respond to the usual anti-epileptic treatments.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has experienced a glue ear in the past.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many individuals with KBG syndrome have had issues with otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient complains of tooth sensitivity, particularly with cold foods.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism and short- or long sightedness.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has trouble digesting certain foods and experiences discomfort during meals.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient requires additional support in school, indicating possible learning difficulties.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Individuals with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, with some children needing support in mainstream settings and others requiring more specialized environments.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has difficulty expressing himself clearly, leading to communication challenges.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many individuals with KBG syndrome have speech delay, with some children acquiring mobility and other skills around the same age as “typical” children and others showing more obvious delay.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has an unusual structure of his spinal bones, which may lead to an increased curvature of the spine.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some individuals with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can give rise to an increased curvature of the spine (scoliosis).

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
a) Recommendations for screening: Regular dental check-ups, regular hearing reviews to age 5, and palatal reviews.
b) Recommendations for treatments: N/A
c) Additional recommendations: Consider review and investigation for tethered cord (MRI) where clinical concerns arise on an individual basis, and monitor growth velocity if height is below the 2nd centile.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s vision or eyes.
Parent: Our son has a tendency to squint, which affects his vision. We've noticed it's more pronounced when he's tired or concentrating hard. The eye doctor said it's something he'll likely grow out of, but for now, we're working on exercises to help strengthen the muscles around his eyes.

Doctor: Please tell us about problems with your child's hearing or ears.
Parent: He gets really frustrated in noisy environments. It's like the sounds overwhelm him, and he becomes irritable. We try to limit his exposure to very loud noises and provide ear protection when necessary.

Doctor: Please tell us about the problems with your child’s teeth.
Parent: His teeth break or chip easily. We've had to take him to the dentist a few times already because of this. The dentist recommended being gentle with his teeth and using a special toothpaste to help strengthen them.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s heart.
Parent: There's a structural abnormality in his heart that we're keeping an eye on. The cardiologist says it's not causing any immediate issues, but we need to monitor it regularly to ensure it doesn't develop into anything more serious.

Doctor: Please tell us about any neurological problem your child has (brain, nerves, muscle tone, fits).
Parent: Unfortunately, he falls more often than other kids. It's not just tripping; sometimes he loses his balance completely. We're working with a physiotherapist to improve his coordination and strength.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child's kidneys.
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s immune system (ability to fight infection and vaccination responses).
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about problems with your child’s gastrointestinal system (feeding, stomach, bowel).
Parent: He experiences bowel problems occasionally. Some foods seem to trigger it, so we're trying to identify and avoid those. Otherwise, his appetite's good, and he eats a wide variety of food.

Parent: Yes, he has undescended testes. The doctors are still running tests to figure out why this is happening and how to proceed. We're waiting for the results and further guidance from the specialists.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a structural abnormality in his heart that requires regular monitoring to prevent potential complications.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences bowel problems occasionally, triggered by certain foods, and has a good appetite despite occasional episodes.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Feeding difficulties and lack of interest in feeding can be significant and long-lasting in some individuals with KBG syndrome.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient falls more often than other kids, indicating poor balance and coordination, which is being addressed through physiotherapy.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, which are typically controlled with anti-epileptic treatments.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss and affect his hearing.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a tendency to squint, which affects his vision and is being monitored and treated accordingly.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Individuals with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism and short- or long sightedness, which may impact their daily life.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences frequent toothaches and cavities, requiring regular dental visits and the use of special toothpaste to strengthen his teeth.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Dental care is crucial, and regular check-ups are essential to prevent further issues.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient needs additional support in school, with some children requiring EHCP and others benefiting from mainstream education.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Education outcomes vary widely, with some children obtaining qualifications and others needing more support.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient exhibits developmental delays and struggles with balance and coordination, affecting his overall physical health and daily activities.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Developmental delay is a common feature in KBG syndrome, with some children acquiring mobility and other skills around the same age as typical children and others showing more obvious delay.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has an unusual structure of his spinal bones, which can lead to an increased curvature of the spine (scoliosis), and short fingers with a curvature of the 5th fingers (clinodactyly).
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A study showed that 11% of children with KBG syndrome have tethered cord, which can cause pain and weakness in the legs, urinary and bowel issues, sacral dimple, and an unusual gait.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
a) Recommendations for screening: Regular dental check-ups, hearing reviews, and palatal reviews.
b) Recommendations for treatments: Monitoring of heart abnormalities, treatment of tethered cord, management of undescended testes, and correction of skeletal anomalies.

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a structural heart abnormality.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has feeding difficulties.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient falls more often than other kids, indicating potential neurological issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, which typically respond to the usual anti-epileptic treatments.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has fluid in his ear.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many children with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has feeding difficulties.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism (the front of the eye is not perfectly rounded, causing blurry vision), and short- or long sightedness (myopia and hypermetropia).

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has weak enamel on his teeth.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Weak enamel is frequently seen in people with KBG syndrome, and careful brushing is very important.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient seems behind other children in development and is not speaking as much as we'd expect for his age.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Education-wise, the situation varies greatly depending on individual circumstances. Some children stay in mainstream education and obtain qualifications, while others may need more support and some benefit from a specialist setting.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient falls more often than other kids and is not speaking as much as expected.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Developmentally, people with KBG syndrome typically have developmental delay and some element of behavioral differences, with speech delay being very common.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has an unusual structure of his spinal bones which can give rise to an increased curvature of the spine (scoliosis).
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 11% of children with KBG syndrome have tethered cord, which can cause pain and weakness in the legs, urinary and bowel issues, sacral dimple, and an unusual gait.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
a) Recommendations for screening: Regular dental check-ups.
b) Recommendations for treatments: N/A

Parent: The dentist mentioned that our child has weak tooth enamel. We make sure to brush his teeth regularly and use a child-friendly toothpaste to help strengthen them.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient requires regular heart health checks to monitor his heart health.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experienced feeding challenges as an infant, with trouble latching on and getting frustrated during meals.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has been slower to reach certain developmental milestones, including walking and sitting, and has shown signs of movement that appears slightly different from peers.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, which typically respond to the usual anti-epileptic treatments.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have feeding difficultyssuch as otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences squint (strabismus), where the eyes do not look in the same direction, and has myopia and hypermetropia.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Individuals with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism and short- or long sightedness.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has frequent dental visits due to weak tooth enamel and needs regular dental care.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Feeding difficulties and lack of interest in feeding can be significant and long-lasting in some individuals with KBG syndrome.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has needed additional support in school, with some children requiring EHCP and others staying in mainstream education.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Education levels vary among individuals with KBG syndrome, with some obtaining qualifications and others needing more support.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has been slower to develop certain skills compared to peers, including walking and sitting.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Developmental delay has been reported in almost all children with KBG syndrome, with some children acquiring mobility and other skills around the same age as “typical” children and others showing more obvious delay.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has an unusual structure of his spinal bones, which can give rise to an increased curvature of the spine (scoliosis), and short fingers with a curvature of the 5th fingers (clinodactyly).
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A proportion of individuals with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can give rise to an increased curvature of the spine (scoliosis).

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
a) Recommendations for screening: Regular dental check-ups.
b) Recommendations for treatments: N/A
